title: Why you remember shocking events so clearly
hook: Traumatic moments create memories that feel like photographs.

narration.text: Emotionally charged events can etch themselves into our minds with surprising clarity.
This phenomenon is called a flashbulb memory, not because of a literal flash.
It is because the event's emotional intensity triggers a powerful biological response.
Adrenaline and stress hormones flood the brain during these moments.
This hormonal surge enhances the memory consolidation process.
The details become more vivid and resistant to forgetting.
These memories often include where you were and what you were doing.
They feel incredibly accurate, but even flashbulb memories can sometimes contain errors.
Have you experienced a flashbulb memory yourself?

description: Ever wonder why you remember every detail of a shocking event? It is not just your imagination. Discover the science behind flashbulb memories and how intense emotions can 'photograph' moments in your mind.
topic: Why you often remember vivid details of emotionally charged events, explaining flashbulb memories.
